text.p: Following are the highlights of the main stories in the Bosnian press on Monday. Reuter has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The World Bank and the governments of Italy, the Netherlands and Canada are sponsoring a $16.2 million de-mining project in Bosnia.

- A group of legal experts from the Moslem-Croat federation published a legal guide which attempts to collect all legal regulations dating back to the old socialist Yugoslav federation to demonstrate evidence of legal continuity in Bosnia.

- A list of inhabitants for the towns of Maglaj and Zavodovici has disappeared from the office of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) in Zepce, where voter registration was held for the second time on Saturday.
- If the privatisation process goes according to a federation government proposal, enterprises will be sold for small sums, Adnan Mujagic, director of the federation privatisation agency, said.
- Council of Ministers delegation pays a three-day visit to Malaysia to discuss economic planning, privatisation, free trade zones and economic cooperation between the two countries.

- Haris Trnka, director of Sarajevo housing administration, denied accusations in Croatian media that 3,000 Sarajevo Croats were prevented from returning to their apartments only because they were Croats.

- The office of the High Representative in Brcko denied allegations in Serb media that Moslem refugees trying to return to this town rejected Serb identify documents and said that it was the Serb authorities who were refusing to issue these documents to the refugees. -- Sarajevo Newsroom, +387-71-663-864
